Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is explicit: CommentThreadBody's new ResizeObserver clears _naturalWidth and fires onDidChangeCommentsSize; CommentThreadWidget forwards onDidChangeContentSize; ReviewFloatingWidget._onContentSizeChanged calls _applySize; _measureContentWidths calls measureNaturalWidth. CommentNode recalculates and lays out its editor when line count changes, providing a concrete typing trigger. The exact duration depends on thread DOM size, but the forced layout and full-subtree allocation are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: cloned DOM nodes and synchronous browser style/layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(thread DOM size) allocation and layout for every comment-element resize at unchanged width, including each edit that changes the embedded editor's line-count height
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked input latency and CPU/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Inline comment widgets did not need natural-width floating-window sizing, so comment editor growth did not clone the full comments subtree or force a max-content offsetWidth measurement.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Floating threads now derive their natural width by cloning the complete comments subtree and synchronously laying out that hidden clone after comment-size changes. Height-only growth while editing invalidates the width cache even though FloatingWidgetSizeModel ignores the natural maximum while isEditing is true.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 53-62 introduce cloneNode(true), temporary DOM insertion, and an offsetWidth read in measureNaturalWidth(); the new floating-widget resize path invalidates this cache whenever the comments element changes size at the same width and immediately re-enters width measurement.
Findings.Title: Avoid cloning the whole thread on edit-height changes
Findings.Impact: In a floating thread with a long discussion, adding or removing lines while editing an existing comment can synchronously clone and lay out the entire thread on the input path. Cost grows with all rendered comments and repeats for each height-changing edit, causing typing latency plus DOM allocation and GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: CommentThreadBody.measureNaturalWidth clones every comment node, appends the clone with width=max-content, and reads offsetWidth. The new ResizeObserver at lines 212-228 clears _naturalWidth whenever the comments element resizes without changing width. ReviewFloatingWidget._onContentSizeChanged synchronously calls _applySize, whose _measureContentWidths path invokes this method before getWidthRange; getWidthRange does not use content.natural when the thread is being edited. CommentNode.calculateEditorHeight/layout changes the comments element height as edited line count changes.
Findings.Recommendation: Separate width invalidation from height-only resize notifications and skip natural-width measurement while isEditing, since getWidthRange ignores it on that path. Recompute the cached natural width only for content changes that can affect width or when leaving edit mode.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The listener lifetime and multiplicity are explicit: _attach adds it per expanded ReviewFloatingWidget and _detach removes it. _render traces directly through code-range geometry, layoutOverlayWidget, SVG path generation, and DOM attribute/style writes. The repository exposes Expand All over every comment widget, making many listeners realistic. Exact frame loss varies with thread count and range size, but the repeated work mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU geometry work plus overlay layout and SVG/DOM writes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(expanded floating widgets × scroll notifications), with additional visible-range line work for commented ranges intersecting the viewport; repeated notifications within one frame repeat the entire render
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased main-thread scroll latency and dropped frames
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Inline zone widgets relied on the editor's view-zone rendering and did not add a per-thread scroll listener that recomputed code geometry and rewrote an overlay connector.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every expanded floating thread now performs its own synchronous geometry and overlay/SVG render on each editor scroll event. Multiple scroll updates before a frame are not coalesced, and Expand All installs this listener for every thread.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 428-432 register one editor scroll listener per attached floating widget and call _render() directly for every horizontal or vertical scroll notification rather than using the class's existing frame scheduler.
Findings.Title: Coalesce floating-widget renders during scrolling
Findings.Impact: With floating style enabled and many threads expanded (including via Expand All), touchpad or smooth scrolling runs one full overlay/connector render per widget per scroll notification. Work scales with expanded thread count and scroll-event frequency, producing main-thread scroll jank and dropped frames.
Findings.Evidence: ReviewFloatingWidget._attach subscribes each expanded widget to editor.onDidScrollChange and invokes _render synchronously. _render calls CommentedCodeGeometry.getLineRects, which scans intersecting visible lines and checks injected text, then calls editor.layoutOverlayWidget and CommentThreadConnector.render; the connector builds an outline path and updates SVG/DOM. The same class already has _scheduleRender, used for model/content changes, but scroll bypasses it.
Findings.Recommendation: Route scroll changes through _scheduleRender so each widget renders at most once per animation frame; preferably share one host-level frame callback across floating widgets and avoid connector geometry work for widgets and ranges wholly outside the viewport.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a commented file or switch comments.thread.experimental.style to floating
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CommentController.beginCompute waits for all registered comment controls to return document comments before setComments creates the selected widget type; expanded floating threads then synchronously measure and attach before display completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request document comments from every registered comment control/provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per registered comment control, issued in parallel for the resource; not per thread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening or recomputing comments already queried every registered provider. The diff additionally makes changing the experimental style invoke the existing beginCompute path once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider promises must settle before the controller receives the full comment-info array and recreates widgets.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered comment providers and returned threads; only threads whose collapsible state is expanded attach floating overlays.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider requests are fan-out promises across controls and join before widget reconciliation; widget creation/display is awaited by the controller paths rather than burst-created in parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new static LRU stores up to 500 layouts keyed by resource, owner, and thread. A warm layout avoids default placement but still measures current content and applies size; provider results are recomputed by beginCompute.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the controller and service call paths and provider cardinality are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count and provider latency vary, but style changes are rare and the diff does not add per-thread provider calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary regression; one pre-existing provider fan-out is newly reached only on an explicit settings change. Floating widget DOM work is evaluated in the scenarios below.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand many floating comment threads and smooth-scroll the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor scroll notification synchronously invokes every attached ReviewFloatingWidget listener; each listener completes code geometry, overlay positioning, and connector SVG updates before returning.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of expanded floating threads (including the existing Expand All command), scroll notifications, and visible lines intersected by each commented range.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All widget listeners execute serially on the UI thread for each notification; there is no shared limiter or animation-frame coalescing on the changed scroll path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-widget line extents cache getOffsetForColumn results until edits/font/layout invalidation, but every scroll still scans geometry, checks injected text, lays out the overlay, and renders connector DOM. No cache coalesces repeated notifications within a frame.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: one listener is installed per attached widget and directly calls _render; Expand All supplies a realistic high-cardinality trigger.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact dropped frames depend on expanded-thread count, range sizes, and input device event rate; the per-widget synchronous multiplicity is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing rendering regression; submitted at commentThreadFloatingWidget.ts:430.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit an existing comment in a long floating thread so the embedded editor grows or shrinks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The comment editor relayout changes the comments element height; ResizeObserver clears the natural-width cache and fires through CommentThreadWidget to ReviewFloatingWidget._onContentSizeChanged, which synchronously measures width and height before input rendering settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered DOM size of the full thread multiplied by edits that change the embedded editor's line-count height or other same-width comment size changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ResizeObserver delivery is asynchronous relative to the mutation but each callback performs the clone and forced measurement synchronously on the UI thread; updates are not coalesced by content key or width relevance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Natural width is cached, but every same-width comments resize invalidates it. While editing, the width model ignores natural width, so the invalidated full-subtree measurement has no sizing benefit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the resize, invalidation, event forwarding, and unconditional measurement call path is fully traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread lengths and frequency of height-changing edits vary, but cloneNode(true), temporary insertion, and offsetWidth forced measurement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous layout/allocation regression; submitted at commentThreadBody.ts:53.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse, dispose, or switch away from floating threads
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collapse detaches overlay widgets, clears attached listeners and scheduled render, and removes connectors; controller/model disposal disposes each widget.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of attached widgets being collapsed or disposed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup runs synchronously per widget; controller loops serialize disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Detached widget resources are released, while only bounded lightweight layout records remain in the 500-entry static LRU for warm recreation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _detach clears listeners/frames and both controller and widget disposal paths are present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for lifecycle correctness; the retained cache bound is explicit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render comment threads in notebook cells or with the default inline style
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Notebook construction passes no floating options, and the default setting selects ReviewZoneWidget, so the new floating geometry, clone-based natural sizing, and scroll listeners are not reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Notebook cell comment widgets or inline editor threads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged widget lifecycle; no new parallel expensive operation from this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The floating-layout LRU and line-geometry caches are not used.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None for reachability; the constructor arguments and default setting are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression on the default inline or notebook paths.
